html:
The Confederated Tribes of Siletz Indians are a union of more than 27 tribes and bands from the coast and valleys of western Oregon, northern California and southwest Washington. The map shows their homelands in 1492.

These peoples spoke at least eleven languages, among them Tillamook, Shasta, Takelma, Kalapuya, Lower Chinook, Coos and several Athabaskan tongues. They lived by salmon, shellfish, acorns and game, in villages of plank houses.

After the Rogue River Wars of 1855 and 1856 the survivors were moved to the Coast Reservation, later called the Siletz Reservation, and the tribes there became one confederation. Settlers took most of the reservation land over the following decades. The federal government ended its recognition of the tribe in 1954; in 1977 Siletz became the first tribe in Oregon to win it back.
